claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you looking to claim Child Benefit for?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do have a child. I'm asking about my son Alex - he's 18 and still lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I understand you're asking about your son Alex, who is 18 and lives at home with you.

Since Alex is over 16, his eligibility for Child Benefit depends on whether he's in approved education or training. 

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he in full-time non-advanced education, such as A-levels, or an approved training program?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. He's currently studying for his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. A-levels at sixth form college would typically count as approved education.

To confirm his eligibility, I need to ask:

**How many hours per week, if any, is Alex working in paid employment?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He doesn't work at all - he's just focusing on his studies at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's very helpful, thank you. Now I need to understand your own circumstances:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Are you the person who is responsible for Alex - meaning you live with him and/or contribute to his upkeep (such as food, clothes, accommodation)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. He lives here with me and I look after him - you know, provide his food, clothes, everything he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for confirming that. Just one final question:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming it for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:
- Alex is 18 years old and under 20
- He's in approved education (studying A-levels at sixth form college)
- He's not working 24 hours or more per week in paid employment
- You live in the UK and are responsible for Alex - you live with him and provide for his needs
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him

Since all the eligibility criteria are met, you should be able to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

**Important note:** You'll normally still qualify for Child Benefit while Alex continues in approved education or training up until he turns 20. However, you would stop getting Child Benefit if Alex were to start paid work for 24 hours or more per week and is no longer in approved education or training.

If you haven't already claimed Child Benefit for Alex, you can make a claim. If you're already receiving it, you can continue to do so as long as his circumstances remain the same.
